wages.text: Opposed a federal rule that would reduce wages for H-2A farmworkers and said agricultural workers deserve protection.
wages.quote: Attorney General Rob Bonta today led a coalition of 17 attorneys general in opposing the U.S. Department of Labor’s (DOL) interim final rule that implements a significant reduction to the Adverse Effect Wage Rate (AEWR ), effectively lowering the wages for workers employed under the H-2A program.

housing.text: Bonta said he would enforce housing laws and require municipalities to allow more homes, including through reforms intended to speed housing approvals.
housing.quote: ensuring that municipalities around the state are building the housing we need

safety.text: Bonta has combined partnerships with law enforcement to address organized crime with efforts to prevent violent crime and support community violence intervention programs.
safety.quote: sought to make California a safer place to call home by partnering with local, state, and federal law enforcement partners to combat organized criminal activity and prevent violent crime before it occurs

sentencing.text: Bonta said arrests and coordinated public-safety programs are preferable to disproportionately lengthy and expensive sentences.
sentencing.quote: a much better deterrent than disproportionately lengthy and expensive sentences

immigration.text: Bonta has challenged federal immigration policies and said his office is defending California’s immigrant communities against mass deportation efforts.
immigration.quote: Attorney General Bonta is committed to defending California’s immigrant communities in the face of the Trump Administration’s inhumane mass deportation agenda.

abortion.text: Bonta has sued to protect emergency abortion care and Medicaid reimbursements for Planned Parenthood health centers.
abortion.quote: Attorney General Bonta remains committed to safeguarding reproductive freedom, protecting access to healthcare coverage, and promoting public health.

gender.text: Bonta joined a brief opposing laws that bar transgender girls from participating in school sports consistent with their gender identity.
gender.quote: Policies that block transgender students from joining sports teams consistent with their gender identity are both discriminatory and unlawful.

cannabis.text: Bonta described California as having a safe, legal, and regulated cannabis market while directing enforcement against illicit cultivation and sales.
cannabis.quote: California has the largest safe, legal, and regulated cannabis market in the world

health.text: Bonta has defended Medi-Cal funding, challenged barriers to ACA coverage, and sued over efforts to end federal Medicaid reimbursements for Planned Parenthood health centers.
health.quote: Blocked the Trump Administration’s attempt to freeze all federal funding to California, including funding for Medi-Cal.

energy.text: Bonta has challenged federal efforts to halt wind energy, electric-vehicle infrastructure, and California’s clean-vehicles program while defending clean-energy funding.
energy.quote: He successfully challenged the Trump Administration’s unlawful attempt to freeze the development of wind energy and is challenging the federal government for its unlawful attempt to upend California’s clean vehicles program.

voting.text: Bonta has opposed federal actions that would interfere with Californians’ ability to vote by mail and said his office is safeguarding voting rights.
voting.quote: We have blocked Trump's attempt to interfere with your right to vote by mail!

tax.text: Gates has said California’s taxes are too high and criticized state officials for considering tax increases.
tax.quote: California has the highest cost of living and the highest taxes, which are crushing families, and Sacramento elites keep scheming for ways to raise our taxes

housing.text: As Huntington Beach city attorney, Gates sued the state over housing mandates and supports local control over zoning and housing policy.
housing.quote: As city attorney, Gates sued the state over housing mandates

safety.text: Gates has pledged to increase police support, enforce existing laws and take a direct role in coordinating with law enforcement officials.

sentencing.text: Gates has pledged to enforce Proposition 36 immediately and criticized state officials for not enforcing it.
sentencing.quote: We’re going to tackle crime. We’re going to be tough on crime, make crime illegal again

immigration.text: Gates has opposed California’s sanctuary policies and said reversing them is the way to keep federal immigration agents out of California neighborhoods.
immigration.quote: He wants federal immigration agents out of California neighborhoods but said the best way to ensure that is to undo California’s sanctuary policies

guns.text: Gates has called local fees and delays for concealed-carry permits unconstitutional and supported local authority over such policies.
guns.quote: local policies, including in Los Angeles County, that charge fees or cause delays in issuing concealed-carry firearm permits, which the Trump administration has sued over and which Gates called unconstitutional

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Gates has opposed transgender girls competing in girls’ sports and brought a lawsuit challenging California limits on schools notifying parents about a child’s gender identity.
gender.quote: He has aligned himself with Trump by backing stricter voter identification laws, alleging massive waste and fraud in state government and opposing transgender kids in girls’ sports.

voting.text: Gates has supported stricter voter-identification requirements and helped file lawsuits seeking voter-registration records.
voting.quote: Gates told LAist he was proud of his work in Washington D.C., in particular with helping to file eight lawsuits seeking voter registration files
